title: don't open chore when overwrite = TRUE?
description: I'm loving the overwrite = T argument!  Thanks.  I was wondering if it might make sense *not* to pop open the chore itself when overwrite = TRUE since the intent is to use a different file as the source for editing. Opening up the registered chore might confuse things (i.e. you start editing there though your intent is to edit elsewhere)  Let me know if this is making sense or if I can clarify further. Thank you!!

title: prompt_new prompt_edit overwrite option
description:
Congrats for chores being up on CRAN! 🚀  Chores is such cool and useful package!  Thank you!!

I just thought I'd pass along, when working with a local file input like 'my_cool_chore.md' as `contents`, I'd want to continue editing that input file, rather than the registered file.  But if felt awkward to do so.  

``` r
prompt_new("boop", "replace", "a_file_with_boop_prompt.md")
```

I'd guess I'd want to be able to do:

``` r
prompt_new("boop", "replace", "a_file_with_boop_prompt.md", overwrite = T)
```
 
and

``` r
prompt_edit("boob", contents = "a_file_with_boop_prompt.md", overwrite = T)
```

Hope that makes sense! 🤷‍♀️🙏

pal addin not working with chat_github (Copilot enabled thanks to GitHub Education pack)
description:
Hi,

Thanks for making `pal`! I was just testing it out and it seems that it doesn't work with `chat_github` as an option. I have GitHub Copilot thanks to my GitHub Education Pack (teacher) and have Copilot configured following https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/tools/copilot.html. This code below does work for me:

```R
library("ellmer")
chat <- chat_github()
live_console(chat)
## Example 1: What is my name?
## Example 2: Who created R?
## Example 3: How many Bioconductor packages are there right now?
## 
## Exit with Q
```

The following doesn't work with `pal`. Note that I've also tried editing the options with my `~/.Rprofile` file (restarting the R session).

```r
library("pal")
options(
  .pal_fn = "chat_github"
)

## Using the pal addin, then selecting "cli" doesn't do anything
rlang::abort("`save_pred` can only be used if the initial results saved predictions.")

## Similarly with selecting "roxygen" with the 3 lines below.
foo <- function(hola) {
    print(hola)
}
```

However, `.init_pal("roxygen")` does work as shown below. So hmm, I'm not sure what's the issue when using the addin or how to provide info that could be useful for debugging this.

``` r
library("pal")
options(
  .pal_fn = "chat_github"
)
pal_roxygen <- .init_pal("roxygen")
#> Using model = "gpt-4o".
pal_roxygen$chat("foo <- function(hola) {
    print(hola)
}")
```

title: support using a custom `base_url` for LLM APIs/ellmer providers
description:
Hi,

Thanks a lot for `pal` (and `gander`). Would it be possible to add support (e.g. via `options`) to use a custom `base_url` for the LLM APIs (the ellmer providers) that support it?

My use case is using `pal`  in an enterprise setting where I need to use a custom `base_url` for the LLM APIs. This works great today with `ellmer` (where I can pass `base_url`  as an argument), but I cannot figure out a way to make `pal`  use a custom `base_url`.

Thanks for your time and effort!

Best,

./ Kristoffer

title: refine streaming experience
description: In the web interfaces for ChatGPT and (especially) Claude chats, the streaming _feels_ super smooth, i.e. responses are pieced together in components even finer than tokens. It feels more "chunky" in pal. This may just be a function of responses from pal tending to be shorter than the few paragraphs typical of an unprompted ChatGPT or Claude, and thus being comprised of fewer total tokens, but I do think a really satisfying interface would make it feel like you're actually watching the model "type."

title: begin streaming before running selection setup
description:
There's a slight delay between clearing all of the current selection and streaming beginning to fill the selection in:

![](https://github.com/simonpcouch/pal/blob/7fe8d97b0dedd5c43c5bd86dec17b54d2953a838/inst/figs/addin.gif?raw=true)

Currently, the addin clears the selection, calls `$stream()`, and then starts the generator. What if we called `$stream()`, cleared the selection, and then start the generator instead?

title: failure modes
description:
- What happens when the input doesn't look like the pal expects? e.g. what if there's no `expect_` in a call to a testthat pal? How would such checks be made available to extensions to implement?
- What happens when output doesn't align with what the prompt specifies the format should be? i.e. if the roxygen pal supplies some text that isn't prefixed with a `#'`.

In these cases, I'm mostly inclined to just say that users ought to Undo, as the process of checking selections and streamed responses seems quite failure prone and it's not that painful to Undo unwanted output.

title: regression with newest Claude Sonnet 3.5
description:
Noticing notably worse output with the newest release from Anthropic a couple days ago. Notably, with the cli pal, the model _really_ wants to add additional bullets, even when they're not needed.

Worth looking into whether one can opt in to older models or whether this kind of effect can be observed with OpenAI's models as well, in which case we ought to iterate on the prompt to emphasize new bullets less.

What actually happens is that both `testthat` and `errors` appear since they both have e's, and which was loaded into the pal env first appears first. :/

title: Positron support

title: figure out + document "addin"-ish functionality in Positron
allow custom prompts
description:
I'm thinking that `pal(role)` will always be an enum _except_ when supplied a connection to a markdown file. That connection could be wrapped with some helper that adds a class so that `pal()` knows not to error out.

e.g.:

```r
# pre-defined option
pal("cli")

# would error out
pal("some_custom_prompt.md")

# works
pal(prompt("some_custom_prompt.md"))
```

title: create a demo pal extension package
description:
Just needs:

* A directory of prompts in `inst/`
* `directory_load()` in `.onLoad()`

Then, link to it here.

title: check `role` more thoroughly
description: I've only been using single strings with no special characters as roles so far. Should we allow for e.g. spaces? Special characters (besides hyphens)? After formalizing, implement a proper check function and test it.

title: test against live API
description: To keep costs down, probably want to test one only one check system and/or only use a really cheap model.

title: clarify meaning of pal/role/prompt
description: Currently, the namespace and documentation use "pal", "role" and "prompt" relatively interchangably, and have various meanings of "add"/"initialize"/"new". This is probably pretty confusing at this point.

title: current addin gif has clipped ending
description: The portion of `inst/figs/addin.gif` where the documentation is written out seems to have been trimmed off the end.

title: relocate `pal_env`
description: The `pal_env` can probably live in the package namespace rather than on the search path.

title: should `pal()` be user-facing?
description:
Starting to feel like the documentation for the package should be relatively independent of the namespace, i.e. not function-by-function. For the most part, we just want users to interface with the addin, and don't need them to use `pal()` or even `pal_add()` directly.

Maybe the main two documentation entries are:

1) Interfacing with the addin
2) Adding custom pals 

...and `pal()` is likely renamed and made internal-ish.

title: hide `pal()` and `$chat()` interface in docs
description: Forefront the addin/tooltip functionality and make the "Pal" objects less of a visual presence.

title: provide registration helper for recommended keybindings
description:
To come after https://github.com/simonpcouch/pal/issues/6.

It'd be great if users could `register_pals()` or something similar, which would

* edit .Rprofile
* add lines a la `pal("cli", "Ctrl + Shift + C")` and whatever other default pals come with the package
* tell users to restart R

There could also be a `register_model()` that does the analogous thing but setting the `.pal_fn` and `.pal_args` arguments so that users could set a persistent default model.

title: mechanism to register keybindings
description:
I think, ultimately, the interface I'd like to have is something like:

```r
pal("cli", "Ctrl+Shift+C")
```

To effectively register keybindings in RStudio, this requires that both:

1) The pal is registered as an add-in
2) The pal is able to bind that add-in to a keybinding

Neither are officially supported in the IDE. 🫠

title: transition key commands interface to snippet
description:
Some feedback: a “snippet” kind of interface (i.e. press one key command that’s common to all pals and then type a keyword, like “cli”) rather than keyboard shortcuts would be better, as there may be eventually too many pals (when extensions are loaded) to easily remember the appropriate key command. That interface is similar to what something like Continue > proofread currently feels like.

Snippet may not be the word I'm looking for here.

title: scope the built-in set of pals
description: The extension mechanism should be really good, and I don't necessary want to be the "keeper of the list." Should the package itself just supply pal roles for package development and document well + encourage extensions for things like authoring and interactive data analysis?

title: don't regenerate output for every `document()`
description:
Right now, every time the one calls `document()`, a bunch of pal requests are sent off—as the package includes more examples, I can imagine this becoming quite costly quite quickly.

For now, I've just been using gpt-4o-mini to keep costs super low (and then intermittently unsetting the `option()` to document with a better model), but that's not a good workflow long-term.

title: change recommended keyboard shortcuts
description:
The package currently recommends `Ctrl+Shift+` some key, but there are many examples of "some key" that are mapped to something else already in RStudio that's painful to undo after mistakenly pressing.

I've been trying chorded shortcuts with `Cmd + ;`—so pressing Command, ;, and r at the same time triggers the roxygen pal, for instance, but is written `Cmd+; Cmd+R`—and have been enjoying it.

title: scoping the testthat helper
description: Currently not super functional but just works to convert to snapshot tests. Should this generally be a "convert to testthat 3" helper, though? Should it be able to take multiple expectations at once?

title: apply new README verbiage where pasted elsewhere
convert pal to R6
description: pals should just be a subclass of elmer Chats with a `$chat` and `$stream` method. The role of the pal may live in a slot inside that object or remain a `Pal` subclass.
